pairs.left: Several hosts in the connection string

pairs.right: The address itself, to another machine

prompt: What do all four approaches have in common at the moment of a failover?

choices.why: Only some read the leader from etcd.

choices.text: They need a restart of the application
choices.why: None needs that; the application reconnects.
Right: no address trick repairs a connection to a server that stopped being primary.

choices.text: They add a network round trip to every query
choices.why: Only a proxy adds a hop.

prompt: Which connection parameter made `psql` settle on the primary among three hosts?
hint: A condition the kept server must meet.

choices.why: Right: it skips servers that refuse writes.
That is about encryption.

prompt: With `target_session_attrs=standby`, which port did the three-host string connect to?
Which cost of client-side lists does the lesson name?
hint: Who has to change when a server is added?

choices.text: libpq sends every query to all hosts
choices.why: It keeps one connection.
It needs nothing in between.

choices.text: It works only for read-only sessions
choices.why: read-write found the primary.

prompt: What does Patroni's REST endpoint `/primary` answer on a replica?

choices.why: Only the leader answers 200.
Right: and 200 on the leader, which is what HAProxy checks.
It does not redirect.

choices.text: Nothing; replicas have no REST port
choices.why: Every node has one.

prompt: Why are `timeout client` and `timeout server` set to 30 minutes?
hint: What does a database connection do most of the time?

choices.text: To give slow queries time to finish
choices.why: Query time is the server's concern, not HAProxy's.
Right: a pooled database connection is idle most of its life.
There is no such minimum.

choices.text: So the health checks have time
choices.why: timeout check covers those.

prompt: Two connections to port 5001 reached 5442, then 5443. Why?

choices.why: pg1 is down on that side because it is the leader.
HAProxy chose; psql had one address.
Nothing failed.
Right: /replica answers 200 on both, and connections alternate.

prompt: What does the lesson say about running a single HAProxy?
hint: It is one more thing that must be up.

choices.text: Run two, or one per application server
choices.why: Right: otherwise the proxy is the new single point of failure.

choices.text: It is enough; it never fails
choices.why: It is one more component to lose.
Then it dies with the primary.
PgBouncer pools; it does not follow the leader by itself.

prompt: How many orders did `orders.sh` report as FAILED during the switchover?
The last order on 5441 was at 02:17:38 and the first on 5442 at 02:17:44. How many seconds took no order?
What happened to the connection that was in the middle of `pg_sleep(30)`?

choices.why: A connection cannot move between servers.

choices.text: It finished its sleep, then failed
choices.why: It was cut in the middle.
Right: terminating connection due to administrator command, when pg1 was stopped.

choices.text: It waited until pg1 came back
choices.why: pg1 came back as a replica; the session was gone.

prompt: Which two things made up the seconds without orders?

choices.text: etcd's ttl and the DNS TTL
choices.why: A switchover does not wait for the ttl, and there was no DNS.
Neither runs before the new primary takes writes.
Those cost a second, not six.
Right: stopping pg1 and promoting pg2, then two good checks two seconds apart.

prompt: An order failed with "connection lost". Why is retrying it blindly risky?

choices.text: The retry goes to the old primary
choices.why: New connections went to the new one.
A new connection accepts them.
Right: it could already have committed; a key chosen by the application makes the retry safe.

choices.text: HAProxy blocks retries for a minute
choices.why: It does nothing of the kind.

prompt: Put what an application should do when its connection breaks in order.
items: Retry it if it did not
trap: Retrying before checking can duplicate an order that did commit.

prompt: Why does a virtual IP often not work in a cloud?
hint: The network decides where an address may live.

choices.why: Right: clouds do not let an address move between machines; a cloud load balancer plays that role there.
They work with IPv4.

choices.text: Patroni cannot run in a cloud
choices.why: It runs anywhere.

choices.text: The address is too slow to move
choices.why: Moving is fast where it is allowed.

prompt: What makes DNS slow to take effect after a failover?

choices.text: DNS records can only change once an hour
choices.why: They change when written.
Right: caches keep the old answer for the TTL at least: resolvers and runtimes, sometimes longer.

choices.text: The new primary has no name
choices.why: The record is changed to name it.
It does, for every host name.
